title: Set instruments on a sterile field and keep them off its unsterile 1-inch border
instruction: Set the instruments out on the sterile field.
context: Surgical technologists and perioperative nurses set up sterile fields before procedures (O*NET 29-2055.00, maintain a proper sterile field during surgical procedures). Aseptic technique taught under AORN and AST standards treats the outer 1 inch (2.5 cm) of a sterile drape or wrapper as unsterile. That edge touches unsterile surfaces and air. Items are delivered to the centre of the field. Anything resting on the border counts as contaminated.
setup: Positions are in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the table top at z 0. The sterile drape is blue fabric, a rigid 3 mm sheet in sim. It is fixed and lies flat on the table over x 20 to 44, y -14 to 22 (24 x 36 cm). The border is not marked. The side-table tray is a fixed grey rigid plastic slab, 30 x 16 x 1 cm (x by y by height), centred at x 22, y -22.5, off the drape. Three instruments lie along x on the tray. They are stainless-steel stand-ins made of rigid bars, each 30 g. The forceps are silver, 12 x 1.6 x 1.2 cm, at x 15, y -18. The clamp is dark steel, 11 x 2 x 1.2 cm, at x 15, y -27. The retractor is light steel, 12 x 2.4 x 1.2 cm, at x 30, y -22.5. Real trials can use the actual instruments, such as closed forceps, a closed hemostat and a small handheld retractor.
scoring: An instrument counts as placed when it lies still and flat (tilted under 20 degrees) directly on the drape, with its whole footprint at least 2.5 cm inside every drape edge. Directly on the drape means its centre is over the drape and its bottom is within 8 mm of the drape's top. Each placed instrument earns one third. An instrument earns nothing if it touches the border band, hangs over an edge, rests on another instrument, stands on its side, is off the drape, or is held. The score is 1.0 when all three are placed. The possible scores are 0, one third, two thirds and 1.0. In a real trial, measure each instrument's nearest point to the nearest drape edge with a ruler at the end. It must be at least 2.5 cm. A photo checks that no instrument rests on another.
reset_notes: Lay the three instruments back on the side tray, each along x, at their start positions. Smooth the drape flat with its edges at the marked positions. Taping the corners to the table stops it from shifting.
fidelity: The drape is a rigid flat sheet in place of fabric draped over a Mayo stand. The instruments are plain bars with no hinges or rings. The simulation uses rigid-body physics only.
